cards.explanation: The answer is True. Sarah, Abraham's wife, bears him a son "…at the very time God had promised." (Genesis 21:2). Not early, not late, right on the dot, friends. Meanwhile I can't pull a batch out of the oven when my own timer tells me to.

The answer is a hundred years old! Genesis 21:5 says Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him. Verse 2 says it happened at the very time God had promised. That's the detail to hold onto, friends.

The answer is everyone who hears of this. Sarah says, "God has made me laugh, and everyone who hears of this will laugh with me." She says everyone who hears, so this is laughter meant to be shared. I think that's joy too big to keep to herself.

The answer is False. Sarah asks, "Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children?" She never says anyone could have. Her next words are, "Yet I have borne him a son in his old age." I think she's still shaking her head at it, friends.

The answer is feast, friends! Genesis 21:8 says Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned. The child grew, and then came the day for the table. I've pulled a few trays out of the oven for a celebration, and I'll tell you what, the cookies were gone before the oven cooled.

The answer is mocking, friends. Genesis 21:9 says Sarah saw that the son Hagar the Egyptian had borne to Abraham was mocking her son. Hagar is Sarah's maidservant (Genesis 16:1), and her son is Ishmael. The text names the mocking, so that's the word we go with.
The answer is True. Sarah tells Abraham, "Expel the slave woman and her son…" (Genesis 21:10). It's a hard thing to say out loud, friends. I think this is one of the heavier parts of the passage.

The reason is that his offspring will be counted through Isaac, friends. God says, "Listen to everything that Sarah tells you, for through Isaac your offspring will be reckoned." The text gives us this reason and no other. God also adds that He will make a nation of Hagar's son (Genesis 21:13), so Ishmael isn't left out.

The answer is False. God says, "But I will also make a nation of the slave woman’s son, because he is your offspring." That's a promise for Ishmael, friends. I think Abraham needed to hear it, since the matter distressed him greatly.

The answer is Beersheba, friends! Genesis 21:14 says Hagar left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba, with bread and a skin of water on her shoulders and the boy with her. Wandering is what the text says she did, and I think that's a long, tiring way to walk. Hold onto that name, because the next part of her story happens out there.

The answer is that she cannot bear to watch him die, friends. She says, "I cannot bear to watch the boy die!" (Genesis 21:16). The text says she sat down about a bowshot away, and that she lifted up her voice and wept. I think that's a mother in deep anguish. This is one of the heavy parts of the story.

The answer is True. The angel says, "Do not be afraid, for God has heard the voice of the boy where he lies." (Genesis 21:17). God heard the boy's voice out there in the wilderness, friends. That's the comfort in the line.

The answer is to lift him up and take his hand, friends. The angel says, "Get up, lift up the boy, and take him by the hand…" (Genesis 21:18). Hagar is told to lift him up and take his hand. After all the weeping, it's a gentle push forward.

The answer is a well of water, friends! Genesis 21:19 says God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. After a skin of water running out, that's about the best thing a person could see out there.

The answer is Egypt, friends! Genesis 21:21 says Ishmael's mother got a wife for him from the land of Egypt. Back in verse 9, the text calls his mother "…Hagar the Egyptian…" So Egypt shows up in both places.
